data.title: Progress
data.tagline: Show how much of a task has been completed
data.description: A progress indicator helps people understand the state of an upload, installation, or multi-step task. Use a percentage when the total is known; otherwise show ongoing activity without pretending to know the finish time. State success, failure, and cancellation clearly.

distinctions.label: Spinner
distinctions.explanation: Progress uses a track to show overall completion and can show a percentage when it is measurable. Spinner usually marks a brief local wait with no known completion ratio.

distinctions.label: Steps
distinctions.explanation: Progress shows continuous completion. Steps names the stages so people know where they are in a process.

avoid: Show a fake percentage when progress is unknown
Leave a completed task stuck below 100%
Use animation without a readable status
Hide failure or cancellation behind the same loading state

lessonPractice.title: A 200MB upload reports uploaded bytes. What feedback should be used?

options.label: Show real Progress percentage or uploaded size, with retry on failure
options.feedback: Correct. When total and completed work are measurable, progress lets people judge the wait.

options.label: Show only a continuously spinning Spinner
options.feedback: When real completion exists, a Spinner loses useful information.

options.label: Immediately show upload complete while it continues in the background
options.feedback: It presents incomplete transfer as success and can lead to data-loss assumptions.

data.agentPrompt: Use real uploaded-byte events to update Progress, showing percentage or size and retaining a retry state for network failure. Upload a test file and interrupt it once; confirm progress follows real events and failure is never shown as complete.
